samples.summary: Every proxy-motivated fix in this delta is asserted only against hand-rolled fake "Yorkie proxies", with no attached-Yorkie test, although that lane exists
samples.evidence: The three behaviours this delta adds all rest on a claim about `@yorkie-js/sdk` proxy semantics: `detachAnchor` (comment-ops.ts:104 — "a Yorkie array proxy is not an array, so the hand walk yields {createdAt,movedAt}"), `withSref`'s `Array.from` (comments.controller.ts:717 — "the Array.prototype method reached through the proxy is not the lookup the engine expects"), and the existing `isThread` array-likeness test. Each is covered only by a literal object the test itself writes: `fakeArrayProxy` (comment-ops.spec.ts:280-288) and `arrayProxy()` (comments.controller.spec.ts:182-186). Those fakes deliberately omit `indexOf` and define `toJSON` as a JSON-string producer, so the tests pass or fail on properties of the fixture, not of the SDK — if a real array proxy does expose a working `indexOf`, or if its `toJSON` differs, the tests still go green while the production claim is wrong. The repo already has the right instrument for this: `packages/backend/test/docs-tree-attached.e2e-spec.ts:1-19` exists precisely because "the colocated spec exercises the pair against an unattached Yorkie document, which bypasses the proxy semantics", and it runs in the `verify-integration` lane. No equivalent attached spec covers comments/anchors (grep for `comments` under packages/backend/test returns only document-copy-attached.e2e-spec.ts). If the proxy assumption is wrong, every comment read on a live doc/PDF document returns a garbage anchor or 500s, and nothing in this suite would notice.
searchedFor: Glob **/node_modules/@yorkie-js/sdk/package.json (SDK not installed, so proxy behaviour could not be confirmed locally)

samples.summary: The prototype-tab-id test enumerates exactly the implementation's own denylist, so it cannot detect the bypass class it claims to cover (`toString`, `valueOf`, `toJSON`)
samples.evidence: The new test loops over `['__proto__','constructor','prototype']` — character-for-character the contents of `UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` (worksheet-images.controller.ts:51). It therefore proves only that a hard-coded set is rejected, not that prototype-shaped tab ids are. On the plain-object fixture used here, `root.sheets['toString']`, `['valueOf']`, `['hasOwnProperty']`, `['isPrototypeOf']` and `['__defineGetter__']` are all truthy functions that sail past `if (!worksheet)` and get `ws.images = {}` written onto them; none of these is in the set and none is tested. The repo's own sibling spec already tests exactly this key: worksheet-structure.controller.spec.ts:74 runs `it.each(['__proto__','constructor','toString'])`, and worksheet-structure.controller.ts:85-96 documents that `toString`/`toJSON`/`getID` are the keys a Yorkie get-trap answers with a truthy function while `__proto__` is safe there by accident — i.e. the images controller's denylist covers the keys that are dangerous only on plain objects and misses the ones dangerous through the proxy. The test presents this as guard coverage.

samples.summary: `detachAnchor`'s catch-fallback and its non-string-`toJSON` path are untested; the latter silently returns the live proxy
samples.evidence: The new comment-ops.spec case only covers the happy `toJSON` path (a proxy whose `toJSON` returns well-formed JSON). Two branches added by this delta have no test: (a) the `catch` at comment-ops.ts:110 — an anchor whose `toJSON` throws or yields an unparseable snapshot should fall through to `detachYorkieValue` rather than 500; (b) the case where `toJSON` returns a non-string, in which `unwrapJson` (yorkie-json.ts:28-33) falls through to `return value as T`, i.e. the live proxy, which passes the `typeof parsed === 'object'` check at comment-ops.ts:109 and is returned undetached — the exact failure `detachAnchor` exists to prevent. Neither is asserted anywhere in comment-ops.spec.ts.

samples.summary: Only the read path is tested with proxy axis orders; `createThread`'s `rowOrder?.[n]` reads never see one in any test
samples.evidence: The new comments.controller.spec case swaps the axis orders for fake proxies *after* `createThread` has already run (comments.controller.spec.ts:176-191), so `srefToCellAnchor`'s reads at comments.controller.ts:653-654 (`worksheet.rowOrder?.[parsed.r - 1]`) are exercised only against real arrays. If numeric indexing on the real proxy behaves differently, thread creation would 400 ("row or column has no id yet") on every live document and no test would catch it. Contained and loud, hence minor.

samples.summary: The chart-repointing test does not assert the foreign chart is copied rather than aliased, and no test covers preservation of a non-pivot `kind`
samples.evidence: `duplicateTab` writes `charts[chartId] = chart` for a foreign-sourced chart (tab-ops.ts:189), sharing the object with whatever the caller passed; the test only compares `sourceTabId` values (tab-ops.spec.ts:229) — the sibling controller test does assert non-aliasing for the worksheet (tabs.controller.spec.ts:306). Separately, the condition changed to `source.kind !== undefined && source.kind !== 'pivot'` (tab-ops.ts:178) and only the `'pivot'` half is asserted; nothing asserts a `'normal'` kind still copies. `SheetKind` is only `'normal' | 'pivot'` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:119), so the blast radius is tiny.

samples.summary: The pivot-drop test asserts what is removed but not the docblock's stated other half — that the materialized cells survive

The test at tab-ops.spec.ts:234-249 asserts only `pivotTable` undefined, `kind` undefined and `resolveDelete`; a `delete copy.cells` regression alongside `delete copy.pivotTable` would pass. Other duplicate tests cover cells for the non-pivot case, so exposure is small.

verdict.reason:
The finding's blocking premise — "if the proxy assumption is wrong ... nothing in this suite would notice" — is false, and the delta's behaviours each have a failure-capable test, so the missing attached-comments spec is coverage narrowing, not a blocking gap.

(1) The tests are not fixture tautologies. comment-ops.spec.ts:92-121 builds a genuine JS `Proxy` that answers `Array.isArray` false (asserted at line 114) and asserts findThread/listThreads still read the thread — it fails if `isThread` (comment-ops.ts:154-159) reverts to `Array.isArray`. comment-ops.spec.ts:284-324 fails if `detachAnchor`'s `toJSON` branch (comment-ops.ts:106-115) is removed, because `detachYorkieValue` (yorkie-json.ts:153-186) would yield `{0,1,length,createdAt,movedAt}` instead of `[{offset:3},{offset:9}]`. comments.controller.spec.ts:169-195 uses an `arrayProxy` that deliberately omits `indexOf`, so deleting `Array.from` at comments.controller.ts:717-718 makes the ref resolution throw.

(2) The SDK-level claims are pinned against the REAL SDK elsewhere in the same, non-gated jest suite: worksheet-charts.controller.spec.ts:89-143 drives `new yorkie.Document` and exercises the exact same `unwrapJson` detach path `detachAnchor` delegates to (worksheet-charts.controller.ts:54-72 vs comment-ops.ts:108), asserting nested `seriesColumns` comes back as a real array that `JSON.stringify` survives; worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:45-51/250/316 asserts numeric `.length` on a real Yorkie array proxy (the `isThread` assumption) and :442-443 spreads a real array proxy (the `Array.from` assumption). If the SDK's object-proxy `toJSON` or array-proxy shape differed, those real-document tests would fail loudly.

It is true that packages/backend/test contains no comments-specific attached e2e (only docs-tree-attached, docs-font-styles-attached, document-copy-attached, the last touching `comments` at lines 47-127 solely for stripping). But under this lens's rubric that is "coverage narrower than it should be while the core behavior is tested" — not a behaviour change lacking any meaningful test, and not fake coverage.

verdict.reason: The images spec's prototype-tab-id test (worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts:103) iterates exactly ['__proto__','constructor','prototype'], which is character-for-character UNSAFE_TAB_IDS (worksheet-images.controller.ts:51). It therefore only confirms the hard-coded denylist and cannot detect the proxy-magic-key bypass class (toString/toJSON/toJS/getID), which this repo itself documents as truthy-through-the-Yorkie-proxy at worksheet-structure.controller.ts:85-90 and tests for the sibling controllers at worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:235-241 and worksheet-structure.controller.spec.ts:74. I searched for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide grep for 'toString'/'valueOf'/'toJSON' literals in packages/backend hits only those two sibling specs; grep for assertPlainTabId/UNSAFE_TAB_IDS finds no shared or broader helper; no global pipe/guard validates :tabId (main.ts:65 ValidationPipe applies to bodies/DTOs); no e2e spec in packages/backend/test touches the /images tab routes; and no other spec instantiates ApiV1WorksheetImagesController. So the images controller's write path (setImages -> root.sheets?.[tabId] then ws.images = {} at lines 83-84,133-139) has no test over the keys that are dangerous through the proxy, while the existing test is presented as guard coverage for that class — a silently weakened guard shipping undetected.
